name: Samantabhadra (Kun tu bzang po), the primordial buddha
summary: In the Nyingma and Bön the dharmakāya primordial buddha, depicted naked and sky-blue in union with Samantabhadrī: the ground recognized as itself. He is the teacher of the Kunjed Gyalpo and the Seventeen Tantras and speaks the Aspiration of Samantabhadra. Distinct from the bodhisattva Samantabhadra of the sūtras (tch:samantabhadra).
alt_names: the Primordial Protector (gdod ma'i mgon po)

realization_account.text: Primordially liberated by recognizing the ground-appearances as his own display, 'without doing even an instant of virtue', and so never entering saṃsāra.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Vajrasattva (Dorje Sempa)
summary: In the Dzogchen transmission the sambhogakāya through whom the teaching passes from Samantabhadra to Garab Dorje; the interlocutor of the Kunjed Gyalpo ('sems dpa' rdo rje'); the deity of purification in the preliminaries (the hundred-syllable mantra).

name: Garab Dorje (Prahevajra)
summary: The first human teacher of the Great Perfection. Born in Oḍḍiyāna to a nun-princess by miraculous conception, he received all the tantras from Vajrasattva, taught the Dzogchen scriptures, and at his passing into light left his testament, the Three Statements that Hit the Vital Point, to Mañjuśrīmitra.

realization_account.text: Realized the Great Perfection from birth; dissolved his body into light and dropped his testament in a golden casket from the sky.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Mañjuśrīmitra
summary: Indian scholar who came to debate Garab Dorje, was defeated, became his disciple for many years, and arranged the Dzogchen teachings into three series (mind, space, instruction); author of the Gold Refined from Ore (Tōh 2591).

realization_account.text: Received Garab Dorje's testament; his own testament was the Six Meditation Experiences.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Śrī Siṃha
summary: Master of the instruction series who, by tradition, was born in China (or Khotan), studied with Mañjuśrīmitra, divided the instruction series into outer, inner, secret and innermost secret cycles, and taught Jñānasūtra, Vimalamitra, Padmasambhava and Vairocana; co-translator of the Kunjed Gyalpo according to its colophon.

name: Jñānasūtra
summary: Disciple of Śrī Siṃha and teacher of Vimalamitra in the instruction-series lineage; his testament is the Four Ways of Leaving as It Is.

name: Vimalamitra
summary: Indian paṇḍita invited to Tibet under Trisong Detsen; he translated the Guhyagarbha and mind-series texts and taught the Heart-essence (Vima Nyingthig) to the king and to Nyang Tingdzin Zangpo, then went to Wutaishan in China. Author of the Simultaneous Entry meditation text in the Tengyur (Tōh 3910).

tradition.text: 8th c.; remains in a body of light at Wutaishan and returns to Tibet every hundred years

realization_account.text: Attained the great transference rainbow body ('ja' lus 'pho ba chen po).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche)
summary: The 'Lotus-born', the second Buddha of the Nyingma. Tradition: born from a lotus on Lake Dhanakośa in Oḍḍiyāna, adopted by King Indrabhūti, a renunciant and charnel-ground yogin who received teachings from many masters, attained immortality with Mandāravā in the Māratika cave, was invited to Tibet by Trisong Detsen on Śāntarakṣita's advice, subdued the spirits obstructing Samye, gave the empowerments of the Eight Herukas to his disciples, concealed treasures for future times with Yeshe Tsogyal, and departed for the land of the rākṣasas, where he dwells on the Copper-Coloured Mountain. Scholarly: an 8th-c. Indian tantric master whose brief stay in Tibet is recorded in early sources; his hagiography grows from the 12th c. treasures.

tradition.text: born miraculously; active in Tibet in Trisong Detsen's reign, when Samye was founded (c. 779)

realization_account.text: Attained the vidyādhara level of immortality and the rainbow body of great transference; appears in eight manifestations.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Śāntarakṣita (Khenpo Bodhisattva)
summary: For the Nyingma, the first of the 'abbot, master and king' (mkhan slob chos gsum): the Nālandā abbot who ordained the first seven Tibetan monks, founded Samye with Padmasambhava and Trisong Detsen, and advised the king to invite Padmasambhava.

name: Trisong Detsen (khri srong lde btsan)
summary: Tibetan emperor (reigned c. 755-797) who invited Śāntarakṣita, Padmasambhava and Vimalamitra, founded Samye and made Buddhism the state religion; for the Nyingma an emanation of Mañjuśrī and a principal disciple and treasure recipient of Padmasambhava.

name: Yeshe Tsogyal (ye shes mtsho rgyal)
summary: Tibetan noblewoman who became Padmasambhava's consort and principal disciple; she compiled and concealed his teachings as treasures, received the Khandro Nyingthig lineage, and is revered as a fully enlightened ḍākinī (the Queen of Great Bliss of the Longchen Nyingthig).

realization_account.text: Attained buddhahood in one life and departed without leaving a body.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

scholarly.text: 8th c. (her full hagiography is a 17th-c. treasure)

name: Mandāravā
summary: Indian princess of Zahor, consort of Padmasambhava, with whom he attained the vidyādhara level of immortality in the Māratika cave; a long-life deity in Nyingma practice.

name: Hūṃkara
summary: Indian vidyādhara of the Eight Herukas transmission to whom the tantras of Yangdag (Viśuddha Heruka, enlightened mind) were entrusted; one of the eight vidyādharas.

name: Buddhaguhya
summary: For the Nyingma, an 8th-c. Indian master of the Māyājāla cycle and commentator on the Guhyagarbha (low confidence on the Nyingma attributions).

name: Vairocana the translator (Pagor Vairocana)
summary: One of the first seven Tibetan monks; sent to India, he received the mind and space series from Śrī Siṃha, translated the five early mind-series scriptures and (with Śrī Siṃha) the Kunjed Gyalpo; exiled through court intrigue to Gyalmo Rong, he taught Yudra Nyingpo there.
alt_names: ba go ra bai ro tsa na

name: Yudra Nyingpo (g.yu sgra snying po)
summary: Vairocana's disciple from Gyalmo Rong, who with Vimalamitra translated the thirteen later mind-series scriptures.

name: Nyak Jñānakumāra (gnyags jñānakumāra)
summary: Translator of the royal period, disciple of Padmasambhava and Vimalamitra, a principal early holder of the Mahāyoga and Anuyoga transmissions and co-translator of the Guhyagarbha.

name: Ma Rinchen Chok (rma rin chen mchog)
summary: One of the first seven monks; translator with Vimalamitra of the Guhyagarbha.

name: Nyang Tingdzin Zangpo (myang ting 'dzin bzang po)
summary: Monk-minister of Trisong Detsen's court and disciple of Vimalamitra who concealed the Vima Nyingthig texts at Zhwa'i Lhakhang; by tradition attained the rainbow body.

name: Namkhai Nyingpo (nam mkha'i snying po)
summary: One of Padmasambhava's twenty-five disciples, a holder of the Yangdag (Viśuddha) heruka practice.

name: Che btsan skyes (Chetsen Kye)
summary: Translator named in the colophon of the Dupa Do as having translated it, with Dharmabodhi and Dānarakṣita, from the script of Bruzha.
notes: Name and role taken from the local colophon of Tōh 829.

name: Nupchen Sangye Yeshe (gnubs chen sangs rgyas ye shes)
summary: Principal early holder of Anuyoga and author of the Samten Migdrön; by tradition he protected the tantric community during Langdarma's persecution by displaying wrathful powers before the king.

tradition.text: disciple of Padmasambhava, living through the persecution

name: Zurpoche Shākya Jungne (zur po che shAkya 'byung gnas)
summary: First of the 'three Zur' who organized the Nyingma kama (Mahāyoga and Anuyoga) transmission and founded Ugpalung.

name: Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo (rong zom chos kyi bzang po)
summary: The greatest early Nyingma scholar, translator and commentator on the Guhyagarbha, author of Entering the Way of the Great Vehicle; counted with Longchenpa and Mipham among the 'three omniscient ones' of the Nyingma.

name: Neten Dangma Lhungyal (gnas brtan ldang ma lhun rgyal)
summary: Recovered the Vima Nyingthig texts concealed by Nyang Tingdzin Zangpo and passed them to Chetsün Senge Wangchuk.

name: Chetsün Senge Wangchuk (lce btsun seng ge dbang phyug)
summary: Heart-essence master of the 11th-12th c. who received the Vima Nyingthig, had visions of Vimalamitra, and by tradition attained the rainbow body; source of the Chetsün Nyingthig revealed later.

name: Zhangtön Tashi Dorje (zhang ston bkra shis rdo rje)
summary: Heart-essence master who recovered further Nyingthig texts and transmitted the Seventeen Tantras.

name: Nyangral Nyima Özer (nyang ral nyi ma 'od zer)
summary: The first of the five 'king' treasure revealers; revealed the Kagye Deshek Düpa, the Copper Island biography of Padmasambhava, and wrote an early history of the Dharma.

name: Guru Chöwang (gu ru chos kyi dbang phyug)
summary: The second 'king' treasure revealer, discoverer of the Kagye Sangwa Yongdzog and the Lama Sangdü, and author of an early account of how treasures are hidden and revealed.

name: Katok Dampa Deshek (kaH thog dam pa bde gshegs)
summary: Founder of Katok monastery in Kham (1159), a centre of the kama transmission; the first of the six 'mother' monasteries in time.

name: Pema Ledrel Tsal (padma las 'brel rtsal)
summary: Revealer of the Khandro Nyingthig; by tradition the rebirth of Princess Pemasal, and Longchenpa was his rebirth.

name: Rigdzin Kumārādza (rig 'dzin ku mA rA dza)
summary: Wandering Heart-essence master, Longchenpa's root teacher, who lived with his disciples in continual encampments.

name: Longchenpa (Longchen Rabjam Drime Özer)
summary: The 'Omniscient' systematizer of the Great Perfection: after monastic studies at Sangphu he received the Heart-essence from Kumārādza and the Khandro Nyingthig, and composed the Seven Treasuries, the Trilogies of Natural Ease, Self-Liberation and Dispelling Darkness, and the Nyingthig Yabzhi; he spent years in Bhutan in exile.

realization_account.text: Reached the final vision of the exhaustion of phenomena; at his death the earth shook and relics appeared.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Orgyen Lingpa (o rgyan gling pa)
summary: Treasure revealer of the Pema Kathang (1352) and the Katang Denga (five chronicles).

name: Karma Lingpa
summary: Treasure revealer of the Zhitro Gongpa Rangdrol cycle, including the Bardo Thödol, found on Mount Gampodar.

name: Rigdzin Gödem (rig 'dzin rgod ldem)
summary: Founder of the Northern Treasures; revealed the Gongpa Zangthal at Zangzang Lhadrak in 1366; named for the vulture-feather-like growths on his head.

name: Sangye Lingpa (sangs rgyas gling pa)
summary: Treasure revealer of the Lama Gongdü (1364).

name: Dorje Lingpa (rdo rje gling pa)
summary: The third 'king' treasure revealer, who also revealed Bön treasures.

name: Tulku Zangpo Drakpa (sprul sku bzang po grags pa)
summary: Treasure revealer of the Prayer in Seven Chapters (14th c.; low confidence).

name: Ratna Lingpa (ratna gling pa)
summary: Treasure revealer who gathered the Old Tantras into the collection from which the Nyingma Gyubum derives.

name: Pema Lingpa (padma gling pa)
summary: Bhutanese treasure revealer, the fourth 'king' tertön, who by tradition revealed treasures from the Burning Lake holding a lit lamp; his lineages and ritual dances shape Bhutanese Buddhism.

tradition.text: the rebirth of Princess Pemasal and of Longchenpa

name: Rigdzin Ngagi Wangpo (rig 'dzin ngag gi dbang po)
summary: Northern Treasure master who re-founded Dorje Drak monastery.

name: Jatsön Nyingpo ('ja' tshon snying po)
summary: Treasure revealer of the Könchok Chidü (the Union of All the Jewels) cycle.

name: The Fifth Dalai Lama, Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso
summary: Gelug ruler of Tibet who was also a Nyingma practitioner and visionary, recording pure-vision treasures (the Sangwa Gyachen) and patronizing Mindroling and Dorje Drak.

name: Karma Chagme (karma chags med)
summary: Master who joined Karma Kagyu Mahāmudrā and the Great Perfection, and whose disciples founded the Palyul tradition.

name: Rigdzin Kunzang Sherab (rig 'dzin kun bzang shes rab)
summary: Founder of Palyul monastery in Kham (1665).

name: Dzogchen Pema Rigdzin (rdzogs chen padma rig 'dzin)
summary: First Dzogchen Rinpoche, founder of Dzogchen monastery in Kham (1685).

name: Terdak Lingpa Gyurme Dorje (gter bdag gling pa 'gyur med rdo rje)
summary: Founder of Mindroling (1676), treasure revealer and compiler of the Nyingma kama; teacher of the Fifth Dalai Lama.

name: Lochen Dharmaśrī (lo chen dharma shrI)
summary: Terdak Lingpa's brother, great scholar of Mindroling, commentator on the Guhyagarbha and on the three vows; killed in the Dzungar persecution of 1717-18.

name: Jigme Lingpa (rig 'dzin 'jigs med gling pa)
summary: Treasure revealer and Dzogchen master who, in three visions of Longchenpa during retreats at Samye Chimphu, received the Longchen Nyingthig; author of the Yönten Dzöd and the Yeshe Lama; at his inspiration the Derge royal house had the Nyingma Gyubum carved, edited by Getse Paṇḍita (moderate).

realization_account.text: Received the mind-transmission of Longchenpa's wisdom body in visions.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: First Dodrupchen, Jigme Trinle Özer (rdo grub chen 'jigs med phrin las 'od zer)
summary: Principal disciple of Jigme Lingpa who spread the Longchen Nyingthig in eastern Tibet.
notes: Lived past 1800 but his formation and main activity began before; not flagged recent (decision logged).

name: Getse Paṇḍita Gyurme Tsewang Chokdrub (dge rtse paNDi ta)
summary: Scholar of Katok who edited the Derge edition of the Nyingma Gyubum and wrote its catalogue.

name: Jigme Gyalwai Nyugu ('jigs med rgyal ba'i myu gu)
summary: Disciple of Jigme Lingpa and Patrul Rinpoche's root teacher, whose oral teaching of the preliminaries Patrul wrote down as the Words of My Perfect Teacher.

name: Do Khyentse Yeshe Dorje (mdo mkhyen brtse ye shes rdo rje)
summary: Mind-incarnation of Jigme Lingpa, a wild visionary yogin and teacher of Patrul Rinpoche.

name: Patrul Rinpoche (dpal sprul o rgyan 'jigs med chos kyi dbang po)
summary: Wandering renunciant master of Kham, speech-incarnation of Jigme Lingpa, famous for simplicity; author of the Words of My Perfect Teacher and the Special Teaching of the Wise and Glorious King; teacher of Mipham and Nyoshul Lungtok.

name: Nyoshul Lungtok Tenpai Nyima (smyo shul lung rtogs bstan pa'i nyi ma)
summary: Patrul Rinpoche's principal Dzogchen disciple.

name: Khenpo Ngawang Palzang (Khenpo Ngakchung)
summary: Katok scholar and Dzogchen master, author of the notes on the Words of My Perfect Teacher (zhal lung zin bris).

name: Mipham Jamyang Namgyal Gyatso ('ju mi pham)
summary: The great Nyingma scholar of the Rimé era, disciple of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Patrul; he wrote commentaries giving the Nyingma its own scholastic curriculum (Madhyamakālaṃkāra, Bodhicaryāvatāra 9, Guhyagarbha, the Beacon of Certainty, the Gateway to Knowledge), argued with Gelug scholars on Madhyamaka, and taught buddha-nature as the union of luminosity and emptiness.

name: Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa (mchog gyur bde chen gling pa)
summary: Treasure revealer of the 19th c. whose treasures, many revealed with Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, were codified by Jamgön Kongtrul (the Chokling Tersar).

name: Dudjom Lingpa (bdud 'joms gling pa)
summary: Visionary treasure revealer of Golok whose Dzogchen treasures include Refining Apparent Phenomena and Buddhahood Without Meditation; many of his disciples are said to have attained the rainbow body.

name: Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo ('jam dbyangs mkhyen brtse'i dbang po)
summary: For the Nyingma, the fifth 'king' treasure revealer, holder of the 'seven transmissions' (bka' babs bdun), who revealed treasures with Chokgyur Lingpa and compiled the Rinchen Terdzö with Jamgön Kongtrul.

name: Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye ('jam mgon kong sprul blo gros mtha' yas)
summary: For the Nyingma, the compiler of the Rinchen Terdzö and of the Hundred Tertöns, and a treasure revealer (Chime Tennyi Yungdrung Lingpa).

name: Adzom Drukpa Natsok Rangdrol (a 'dzom 'brug pa)
summary: Dzogchen master and treasure revealer of Kham, disciple of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Patrul Rinpoche.

name: Tertön Sogyal Lerab Lingpa (gter ston bsod rgyal las rab gling pa)
summary: Treasure revealer, teacher of the Thirteenth Dalai Lama.

name: Dudjom Rinpoche Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (bdud 'joms 'jigs bral ye shes rdo rje)
summary: Reincarnation of Dudjom Lingpa, treasure revealer, historian of the Nyingma (Fundamentals and History), editor of the enlarged Kama, and the first head of the Nyingma school in exile.

name: Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche Tashi Paljor (dil mgo mkhyen brtse)
summary: Nyingma master and treasure revealer, holder of the Longchen Nyingthig and Rimé lineages, later head of the Nyingma school; transmitted the Rinchen Terdzö many times.

name: Chatral Sangye Dorje (bya bral sangs rgyas rdo rje)
summary: Renunciant Dzogchen master, disciple of Khenpo Ngakchung; lived in retreat in the Himalaya.

name: Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok ('jigs med phun tshogs)
summary: Treasure revealer and founder of the Larung Gar academy in Serthar.

name: Chögyal Namkhai Norbu (nam mkha'i nor bu)
summary: Dzogchen master and scholar who taught Dzogchen internationally (the Dzogchen Community) and wrote on Bön and Zhang Zhung history.

name: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (sprul sku o rgyan)
summary: Holder of the Chokling Tersar and Dzogchen teacher in Nepal.

name: Tönpa Shenrab Miwoche (ston pa gshen rab mi bo che)
summary: Founder of Yungdrung Bön. Tradition: a fully enlightened teacher who descended from the heavens and was born prince of Ölmo Lungring in Tagzig; he taught Bön, pursued into Tibet the demon Khyapa Lagring who had stolen his horses, taught there and returned; his deeds are told in the Dodü, the Zermig and the Zijid.

tradition.text: born in 16,017 BCE by a traditional Bön reckoning

name: Drenpa Namkha (dran pa nam mkha')
summary: Great Bön master of the 8th c., who by Bön tradition upheld Bön under Trisong Detsen and concealed texts; the commentator of the Sipai Dzöpuk; figures also in Nyingma accounts (low confidence on details).

name: Tapihritsa (ta pi hri tsa)
summary: Zhang Zhung master of the Nyengyü lineage who attained the rainbow body and later appeared as a boy to Gyerpung Nangzher Löpo to transmit the Oral Transmission; visualized as a naked, crystal-white figure in guru yoga.

realization_account.text: Attained the rainbow body; returned as an emanation to teach.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Gyerpung Nangzher Löpo (gyer spungs snang bzher lod po)
summary: Zhang Zhung master of the 8th c. to whom Tapihritsa transmitted the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü, which he set down.

name: Shenchen Luga (gshen chen klu dga')
summary: Principal Bön treasure revealer (discoveries of 1017), from whose disciples descend the great Bön families (Dru, Zhu, Pa).

name: Meu Gongdzö Ritrö Chenpo (rme'u dgongs mdzod ri khrod chen po)
summary: Bön master credited with the A-tri system of Dzogchen meditation.

name: Dru Gyalwa Yungdrung ('bru rgyal ba g.yung drung)
summary: Bön master credited with the practice manual of the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü and with arranging the A-tri.

name: Loden Nyingpo (blo ldan snying po)
summary: Bön master through whom the Zijid, the long biography of Tönpa Shenrab, was transmitted.

name: Nyamme Sherab Gyaltsen (mnyam med shes rab rgyal mtshan)
summary: Founder of Menri monastery (1405), the principal seat of Yungdrung Bön monasticism.

name: Shardza Tashi Gyaltsen (shar rdza bkra shis rgyal mtshan)
summary: Bön Dzogchen master and prolific author of Kham (history of Bön, Dzogchen manuals), who by tradition attained the rainbow body at his death.

realization_account.text: His body shrank and dissolved into light at death (rainbow body).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Lopön Tenzin Namdak (slob dpon bstan 'dzin rnam dag)
summary: Bön scholar and Dzogchen master who re-established Bön monastic education in exile (Dolanji, Triten Norbutse) and taught the Zhang Zhung Nyengyü widely.

name: Lungtok Tenpai Nyima, 33rd Menri Trizin (lung rtogs bstan pa'i nyi ma)
summary: Abbot of Menri in exile (Dolanji), spiritual head of Bön.
